e40158c23d19d3d4: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The Selangor government is considering whether to appeal a High Court ruling that found the federal government and two state authorities liable for negligence over the devastating 2021 Taman Sri Muda floods.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the state would first seek advice from the State Legal Adviser before deciding its next step, Berita Harian reported today.
“(We will examine) whether an appeal should be filed or otherwise, because this is only a High Court decision and there is still room for an appeal to provide justification,” he was quoted as saying.
He was speaking after the launch of the Selangor Roads and Highways Strategic Plan 2026-2035 (JALUR Selangor) here.

The High Court yesterday ruled in favour of 50 Taman Sri Muda residents who sued the government and several public authorities over losses they suffered during the catastrophic floods in December 2021.

Judicial Commissioner Shoba Rajah Dorai Rajah found the federal government, the Selangor Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) and Shah Alam City Council (MBSA), among the defendants, liable for negligence and related failures that contributed to the residents’ losses.
The residents alleged failures in flood management, drainage systems, weather warnings and disaster response.
The court held the liable defendants jointly and severally responsible for the losses suffered by the residents.
The residents are seeking RM3,767,148.51 in special damages, as well as general and aggravated damages.
The High Court has fixed October 6 for case management to determine a date for the assessment of damages.
Taman Sri Muda in Shah Alam was among the areas worst affected by the widespread floods of December 2021, which left residents stranded as floodwaters rose rapidly.
47278107674cd8ef: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The haze currently affecting the country is caused by moderate to thick smoke from clusters of hotspots detected across much of Kalimantan as well as central and southern Sumatra.

Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) reported 327 hotspots in Kalimantan and another 191 in Sumatra yesterday, while one hotspot was detected in Sarawak.
“ASMC also reported moderate transboundary haze affecting several areas in Peninsular Malaysia, Singapore and northwestern Borneo,” she said in a statement today.
She said the DOE had stepped up inspections, patrols and monitoring in fire-prone areas, particularly peatlands and landfill sites, amid continued hot and dry weather.
“Where offences are identified, follow-up action will be taken based on the findings of inspections and investigations, as well as evidence obtained on the ground,” she said.

Azuri Azizah said the DOE would continue monitoring Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, hotspots and transboundary haze developments, taking meteorological information into account when assessing the situation and coordinating haze management measures at district, state and national levels.

As of 2 pm today, 23 areas in Peninsular Malaysia recorded unhealthy API readings, with the highest readings reported in several states, including Selangor, Johor, Negeri Sembilan and Pahang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.

She said DOE measures were being carried out in an integrated manner under the National Haze Action Plan (PTJK), which sets out the roles of various agencies according to the severity and development of the haze situation.

The department would also regularly provide updates on the situation, monitoring and patrol findings, Open Burning Prevention Operations (OMPT) and enforcement actions in accordance with the established reporting mechanism.
She said this was to ensure the situation could be assessed continuously and appropriate measures coordinated at all levels.
The DOE also stressed the need for cooperation from the industrial sector to reduce air emissions from major sources, particularly in areas where API readings exceed 300. — Bernama
0d900d50e42b9362: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia imposed administrative monetary penalties (AMPs) of RM22,000 on Wawasan Ilham (M) Sdn Bhd (WISB) and RM6,900 on SMJ Teratai Sdn Bhd for failing to comply with customer due diligence (CDD) requirements.
Bank Negara said it discovered the breach following an on-site supervisory examination of WISB.

"During the examination, it was found that WISB had failed to conduct CDD on a customer for a money-changing transaction due to inadequate oversight and weak compliance culture," it said in a statement.
The central bank noted that it also discovered the breach following a supervisory examination of SMJ Teratai.

"During the examination, it was found that SMJ Teratai had failed to conduct CDD on a customer for money-changing transactions due to a lack of reasonable care in implementing the CDD requirement by its staff," it said.
Meanwhile, Bank Negara also imposed an AMP of RM11,500 on Ruhanmas Forex Sdn Bhd for failure to comply with targeted financial sanctions requirements.
It said Bank Negara discovered the breaches following an on-site supervisory examination of Ruhanmas.
"During the examination, it was found that Ruhanmas had failed to maintain a sanctions screening mechanism and to conduct sanctions screening on its customers.
"These breaches were attributed to Ruhanmas' lack of understanding of applicable regulatory requirements," it added.
All the companies have paid the penalties.
5e96940175b63152: PUTRAJAYA: The cabinet has prayed for the health of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, who is under observation at the National Heart Institute (IJN),
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the cabinet also recorded its condolences to Dr Mahathir and his family following the passing of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali.
"First, the prime minister, the cabinet and the government record their condolences to Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and family on the passing of Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, may Allah bless her soul.
"She was a highly respected woman leader and stateswoman," he said at a post-Cabinet meeting press conference here.
ccdd78230c13a62d: SHAH ALAM: PH sees room for cooperation with any party or coalition, including BN, in the Melaka election.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said he had met PKR leaders in Melaka yesterday and heard views from PH Melaka.
He said a meeting with BN would be held soon to explore possible areas of cooperation.
"There are strategies that need to be considered if both coalitions work together.
"I need to finalise the matter with the PKR central leadership council so that we can make a policy decision on the next step.

"Either we contest under a common understanding with several parties, or we focus on our respective areas while reaching agreements with certain parties," he told reporters after the launch of the Selangor Road and Highway Strategic Plan 2026-2035 (Jalur Selangor) here today.

Earlier, media reports quoted BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki as confirming that negotiations and discussions on the coalition's direction for the Melaka election were still ongoing.
Asyraf was reported to have said that any developments remained at the negotiation stage among the leadership.
762b62211eb9399c: KUALA TERENGGANU: A policeman pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to four charges of accepting bribes amounting to RM2,400 four years ago.

Roslee Mamat, 43, a sergeant major with the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division at the Setiu Police headquarters, was charged with accepting bribes ranging from RM400 to RM1,000 from an individual as an inducement to provide advance information on police operations or raids, thereby enabling the individual to take precautionary measures or flee to avoid arrest.
The offences were allegedly committed at a bank branch in Shah Alam, Selangor, and Masjid Gong Terap in Setiu in October and December 2022.

The charges were framed under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009, punishable under Section 24(1) of the same act, which carries a maximum prison term of 20 years and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the bribe, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
Judge Azman Mustapha set bail at RM6,000 in one surety and fixed Oct 27 for mention.
Roslee was also ordered to surrender his passport and report to the MACC office every month.
MACC deputy public prosecutor Nur Amalina Najwa Mohd Ali prosecuted, while Roslee was represented by lawyer Mohd Fakhrul Fikri Mokhtar.
cfd5ddc2adc5ea81: NAGOYA: Under 1,000 spectators watched Asian Games hosts Japan beat South Korea in the semi-finals of the women's football at a 50,000-capacity stadium, with a top official admitting Wednesday that attendances at some events were "disappointing."
Japanese organisers have been on the defensive over ticket sales since the opening ceremony on September 19 took place in front of thousands of empty seats in Nagoya.
Officials said on that occasion that the threat of a typhoon put people off, and heavy rain fell from Sunday until Tuesday this week.
While some competitions have played out to healthy crowds, others have struggled to attract fans.
Tuesday's first women's football semi-final at the stadium in Shizuoka, a venue for the 2002 FIFA World Cup, saw North Korea beat China 2-0 in front of an official attendance of 564.
With rain falling steadily, 998 people then saw the hosts defeat South Korea by the same scoreline.
Japan and North Korea will meet for gold on Friday at the same stadium.
Takashi Yamazaki, head of ticketing, told reporters on Wednesday: "Sports that are selling well are... at 80 percent or 90 percent or more."
But he added: "On the other hand, the large venues for baseball and football, as well as athletics, have struggled from the start because of their size.
"Tickets usually surge in the final stretch before an event.
"But as you know, there was a long spell of cold rain, and sales stalled.
"We were already struggling more than expected, and then sales stalled further.
Organisers in Aichi-Nagoya said Tuesday that more than one million tickets had been sold for the continent's biggest sporting spectacular.
But they also admitted they were "not satisfied" after the men's and women's 100m, the blue-riband athletics events, took place in front of thousands of empty seats on Friday.
676be7939ac4865f: PUTRAJAYA: Nepal has agreed to help expedite the process of confirming the status of 55 Malaysians who remain untraced following the disaster in the country, said government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Fahmi said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had spoken to his Nepali counterpart yesterday, during which the latter agreed to the request.

"Nepal's prime minister has informed of his agreement to help speed up the process of confirming the status of the 55 Malaysians who remain untraced following the disaster in Nepal," he told reporters at a post-Cabinet meeting press conference here.
He said Anwar had directed the attorney-general to hold further discussions urgently with the relevant Nepali authorities to expedite the process.
4ddbc6f537e5a815: KUALA LUMPUR: GXBank has called for the expansion of government-backed credit guarantees to digital lending platforms as part of efforts to improve financing access for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) under the 2027 Budget.

Its chief executive officer Kaushik Chowdhury said expanding guarantee schemes, including the proposed RM10 billion Bank Negara Malaysia-Credit Guarantee Corporation facility, to digital lenders would allow them to provide lower cost loans to MSMEs.

"By leveraging alternative underwriting data, such as real-time cash flows and e-commerce transactions, digital banks can safely deploy low-cost, collateral-free working capital to small businesses facing severe margin pressures," he said in a statement.
Kaushik said the 2027 Budget also presents an opportunity to reduce administrative and other frictions associated with micro-financing.

Building on the stamp duty relief for micro-financing introduced in the 2025 budget, he proposed extending targeted duty exemptions to small-ticket loans to reduce the disproportionate costs associated with lower-value borrowing.
"Digital banks can seamlessly pass these tax savings directly to hawkers, gig workers and MSMEs - lowering effective borrowing costs," he added.
Kaushik also called for greater integration between licensed digital banks and government digital infrastructure through direct, low-cost application programming interface connections.

Streamlining digital verification would reduce onboarding requirements and operational costs while expanding access to financial services among rural communities, gig workers and underserved groups, the digital bank said.
Separately, Kaushik proposed tax incentives and public matching grants for financial institutions investing in artificial intelligence-based fraud detection and scam prevention.
"Treating anti-scam protection as shared critical infrastructure ensures banks can maintain robust security without passing technology overhead costs down to lower-income consumers," he said.
61764cf13d6f6613: British Transport Police (BTP) spent more than £320,000 putting half a million commuters through live facial recognition cameras, only for the system to identify precisely nobody it was looking for. Figures obtained by civil liberties group Liberty through Freedom of Information requests, and reported by The Guardian, show BTP's six-month trial scanned more than 500,000 faces at London railway stations and generated just one alert. That turned out to be a false positive, meaning the technology produced no correct matches and no arrests directly resulting from an LFR alert. The exercise wasn't exactly light on resources either. According to the figures, deployments swallowed almost 100 hours of police officers' time and cost more than £320,000. Privacy campaigners at Big Brother Watch told The Register the results would be funny if the implications weren't more serious. "The figures from the British Transport Police's live facial recognition pilot would be laughable, if they didn't have such troubling implications for our rights and freedoms," said Jasleen Chaggar, senior legal and policy officer at the campaign group. "Millions of Londoners use the city's stations every day and may have already found themselves caught in a digital police line-up, likely without even realizing." Then there's the small matter of what taxpayers got for their £320,000. "It's not fair to subject innocent people to intrusive identity checks during their commute, but it's even more insulting to waste almost 100 hours of officers' time and £320,000 of public money when it produces such meagre results," she said. "The pilot figures show that replacing officers with AI surveillance does not improve Londoners' safety and British Transport Police should drop their use of live facial recognition." But BTP isn't dropping it. In fact, the trial has been extended until November and expanded from Network Rail stations onto the London Underground. The system uses NEC's NeoFace M40 facial recognition tech, and cameras scan people passing through a designated area, comparing their faces against a police watchlist. When the software thinks it has spotted someone on that list, it generates an alert for an officer to review before deciding whether to stop the person. BTP says it cannot identify people who aren't on a watchlist and that it immediately deletes their biometric data. It also says deployments are intelligence-led and targeted at crime hotspots where officers believe "high harm offenders" are likely to pass through. That claim of a targeted approach isn't convincing everyone. Sarah Simms, senior policy officer at Privacy International, told The Register the results of the trial show just how many innocent passers-by can have their faces processed along the way. "We are deeply concerned by the results of the British Transport Police's live FRT trial. It reaffirms how invasive and disproportionate live facial recognition tech is and why it shouldn't be permitted. Thousands of people have their highly sensitive facial data processed in public spaces as they go about their daily lives, sometimes unknowingly. It also undermines claims of it being a targeted measure." Simms also pointed to the lack of legislation specifically governing the technology as BTP continues to expand its use. "What's further concerning is that they continue to extend these deployments when there is no specific legal framework in place to regulate facial recognition, which is essential to ensure there are restrictions and safeguards on its use to protect people's rights," she said. Those assurances haven't put the wider controversy around police facial recognition to bed. Earlier this year, UK police temporarily suspended deployments after independent testing raised concerns about racial bias at some operating thresholds. BTP's own experiment has produced a rather different problem so far: after scanning more than half a million faces, the only person its cameras picked out was the wrong one.®
6bfb78409efa6f1a: PUTRAJAYA: A total of 3,542 Myanmar detainees have been agreed for repatriation in the second phase, following the return of 1,476 people in the first phase yesterday.
Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the 1,476 detainees in the first group had been identified by the Myanmar authorities.
He said their names were submitted to Malaysia through a diplomatic note dated Aug 13 via Wisma Putra.
"For the second phase, 3,542 Myanmar detainees have been agreed with Myanmar to be sent home at the next stage," he said at a post-Cabinet meeting press conference here.

There are pensioners out there who watch your programme who are paying for care costs from their basic state pension. Now, is that right or fair? Continue reading...
b02d887a43dc55e0: WASHINGTON: US Senate Republicans on Tuesday blocked a bid to require President Donald Trump's administration to report to Congress on increasing violence in the occupied West Bank, including the deaths of American citizens.

The procedural vote was the latest sign of friction between US Democrats and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government over Israel's treatment of Palestinians and of Republicans' continuing strong support for his coalition.
The Senate voted 47 to 51 to block the resolution.
The vote was largely along party lines, with every Republican voting no except for Rand Paul of Kentucky and every Democrat except John Fetterman of Pennsylvania in favor.

The resolution would have required the State Department to report to Congress on the killing of US citizens by Israeli settlers or Israeli security forces in the West Bank and to assess the human rights situation.
Violence by Jewish settlers against Palestinians in the territory has risen sharply this year.

While the resolution would not have cut aid to Israel, the largest cumulative recipient of US foreign assistance since World War Two, a failure by the administration to deliver the report could have triggered restrictions on aid.

Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, the measure's lead sponsor, had argued that it was "long past time" to examine human rights in the West Bank, including the deaths of nine Americans since 2022.
"It is our responsibility to ensure recipients of US taxpayer dollars act in line with our laws and our values," he said in a statement, referring to Israel.
Republicans accused Democrats of seeking to score political points as Israel is under threat, seven months after US and Israeli forces launched airstrikes that began an ongoing conflict with Iran.

"I urge my colleagues to vote no on this resolution so we can stand with our ally Israel as they beat back the scourge of Iranian-backed terrorism," Montana Republican Senator Steve Daines said in a speech.

The vote took place weeks before US midterm elections on Nov 3, in which polls show Trump's Republicans could lose their congressional majorities, signaling a potential shift in Israel policy in the new Congress.
Polls show the war with Iran is not popular with Americans, who are frustrated with higher energy prices resulting from the conflict.
Netanyahu, who has long aligned himself with US Republicans, faces an election in Israel on Oct 27, which public opinion polls show his right-wing coalition could lose.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. The UN and most countries consider settlements there illegal under international law governing military occupation. Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied.

Some Democrats — and a few ​Republicans — also have called for curbs on military aid to Israel over its conduct of the war in Gaza, with tens of thousands of Palestinians killed and much of the enclave in ruins.
3d3f99187618c43d: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — Pakatan Harapan has yet to begin formal discussions with Bersatu over possible cooperation for the Melaka state election, despite a closed-door meeting between representatives of both sides earlier this week.

PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said any decision on political cooperation would have to be made by the coalition's presidential council, adding that he had not received any information on formal negotiations with Bersatu.
“So far, there have been no developments (on the cooperation). I have yet to receive any information on the matter,” he told reporters yesterday.

His comments came after PH and Bersatu leaders attended a closed-door dinner in Melaka on Monday night, fuelling speculation that the two sides could be exploring an electoral arrangement ahead of the state election.

However, acting Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abdul Halim described the gathering as an opportunity to maintain cordial ties, while Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz said it was an informal session to get to know one another and exchange views.
PH has also indicated that it is open to discussions with other parties, with Adam saying the coalition was still waiting for PAS to extend an invitation for talks.
“PAS is the only one that has not invited us yet and I am waiting too,” he was reported as saying.

The developments come as political parties consider their respective electoral arrangements before the Election Commission meets on October 7 to determine key dates for the 16th Melaka state election.
The EC said the special meeting will decide, among other matters, the writ of election, nomination day, polling day and the electoral roll to be used.
The Melaka state assembly was dissolved on September 23.

46010f0fe75a6d3f: NAGOYA: The Speedy Tigers must maintain their relentless momentum and guard strictly against South Korea's lethal penalty corner threat when both sides lock horns in the semi-finals of the men's field hockey competition at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Thursday.
That is the view of national team manager Datuk Ahmad Najmi Abdul Razak.
Malaysia sailed through the group stage in imperious form, firing in 34 goals while conceding just four times to top Group B.
Ahmad has urged the squad to remain vigilant against a disciplined and dangerous Korean side.

He stressed that maintaining their high standards from the group matches is paramount as the squad targets a spot in the final and a shot at direct qualification for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games.
"Our expectation, of course, is for the team to carry forward the great momentum built during the group stage and push through to the final," said Ahmad.
Tactically, Ahmad pinpointed defensive discipline in transition and strict coverage as the keys to keeping Korea's forward line at bay.

"We cannot afford to give them large spaces or leave players isolated in one-on-one situations. We need to ensure we consistently double-team to restrict and contain Korea's attacking moves," he stressed.
Malaysia go into the match as the higher-ranked side, world No. 14, while Korea are No. 19.
But Korea's set-piece expertise remains an ever-present danger that could quickly turn the game on its head.
Ahmad highlighted Korea's deadly set-pieces as the primary threat Brendon Carolan's side must neutralise throughout the 60 minutes.
"Although Malaysia hold a higher ranking, Korea are certainly no lightweights. We must be particularly wary of their penalty corners, which are always a major threat to our side," Ahmad warned.

Former national captain Datuk Mirnawan Nawawi echoed similar sentiments on Tuesday, cautioning the national team against underestimating Korea, who earned their semi-final berth by knocking out host nation Japan in the pool matches.
A victory will move the Speedy Tigers within one step of booking an automatic ticket for LA 2028.
Only the gold medallists in the men's and women's event will gain direct entry to Olympics.
e464c243ee8f9fa6: SEREMBAN: Ten former Negri Sembilan executive councillors whose appointments were revoked have stopped using their offices at Wisma Negeri and returned their official vehicles.
The move followed the gazetting of the revocation of their appointments on Sept 24, which took effect from Sept 20.

Former state Industry, Technology, Innovation and Digital Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, speaking on behalf of the former executive councillors, confirmed that they had received instructions from the State Secretary's Office to return their official vehicles.
"Since the gazette was issued, I have no longer used the official vehicle.
"We received a letter from the State Secretary instructing us to return the vehicles.
"We complied with the directive. Whatever the instruction is, we will follow it," said Asna, who is also Lenggeng assemblyman.
However, the former executive councillors' offices at Wisma Negeri continue to operate, with their officers and staff remaining at work.
"The former executive councillors no longer come to their offices at Wisma Negeri.
"All the assemblymen are operating from their respective state constituency service centres.
"Only we, the officers and staff, continue to carry out our duties here at Wisma Negeri," an officer attached to one of the former executive councillors said when contacted today.
The appointments of the 10 executive councillors were officially revoked with effect from Sept 20 with the consent of Negri Sembilan Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
The revocation was gazetted on Sept 24.

According to the gazette, the appointments were withdrawn after the 10 were found to have breached their pledges of allegiance following their actions in relation to a proclamation concerning Tuanku Muhriz's position as Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Police officers from Bukit Aman police recorded statements from the 10 former executive councillors as part of investigations into the matter.
Yesterday, Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim had an audience with Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Hinggap Seremban.
The meeting was understood to be related to the state administration and the ongoing situation.
Ismail has yet to issue any statement on the substance of the meeting or whether any decision was reached.
His press secretary, Mohd Fasha Musthafa, said there had so far been no instruction to issue a statement.
6c59a752dcc322e2: GEORGE TOWN: Thirty-four Flowerhorn fish were seized after authorities detained a man suspected of selling prohibited fish online.
The Department of Fisheries (DoF), through its Conservation and Fisheries Protection Branch (CKOPP), conducted the enforcement operation with police following a complaint about the sale.
The Penang Fisheries Office said 10 CKOPP officers and three police personnel were involved in the operation.
"Ten CKOPP officers and three police personnel successfully detained an individual suspected of being involved in the online sale of prohibited fish," it said in a Facebook post yesterday.
The case is being investigated under the Fisheries Regulations (Prohibition Species etc., for Fish) (Amendment 2024).
DoF said it would continue intensifying monitoring and enforcement against the sale of prohibited fish, including through various social media platforms.
It said the efforts were aimed at ensuring compliance with the law while protecting the country's fisheries resources and aquatic ecosystems.
In Malaysia, the sale, possession or import of prohibited and invasive alien fish species is regulated under the Fisheries Act 1985 and related regulations.
Those found possessing prohibited fish without approval can face a fine of up to RM100,000 under the Fisheries Act 1985.
30361d42d2016b31: NAGOYA: South Korea struck with eight minutes left to seal a 2-1 victory over a heartbroken China on Wednesday and reach the final of the Asian Games men's football.
They will face either hosts Japan or Uzbekistan for gold on Saturday.
Bae Jun-ho was the hero for the South Koreans, ghosting in at the back post to head in a dramatic 82nd-minute winner at Nagai Stadium.
China's men have never won Asian Games football gold and were contesting their first semi-final since 1998.
History looked on the cards when Wang Yudong finished off a smart team move with an emphatic finish to put China ahead on 22 minutes.
In an entertaining encounter in front of a sparse crowd, Lee Young-jun hit back for South Korea 11 minutes later with China goalkeeper Li Hao getting a hand to it but unable to keep the ball out.
China had several good chances in the second half to retake the lead, before Stoke City's Bae popped up with the winner.
North Korea will face Japan in the women's final.-AFP
751fa9a302431fa7: KUALA LUMPUR: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) passenger train services between Batang Benar and Labu stations are facing a disruption following a 25kV overhead line equipment fault at 6.24am today.
KTMB said an initial inspection found that the incident was suspected to have been caused by an animal coming into contact with the live wire and earth wire.
"Under normal operating conditions, these two components should not have a direct electrical connection.

"When an animal comes into contact with both simultaneously, it can create an unintended path for electrical current, triggering an interruption to the protection system and power supply of the overhead line equipment," it said in a statement today.
It said the disruption had affected train operations along the route, resulting in delays to several services.
Some services also had to terminate earlier to allow inspection and recovery work to be carried out safely.
The incident also affected Electric Train Service (ETS) and KTM Komuter operations on the Batu Caves-Pulau Sebang-Batu Caves route.
"Following the incident, several operational adjustments have been implemented, including for ETS services from JB Sentral to KL Sentral.
"Trains will terminate at Seremban station, where passengers will be transported by bus to KL Sentral and intermediate stations.
"For passengers travelling from KL Sentral to JB Sentral, they will be transported by bus to Seremban station before continuing their journey to their destination," it said.
ETS passengers will also be provided with shuttle buses at KL Sentral, Bandar Tasik Selatan and Kajang to Seremban station.
From there, they will continue their journey by ETS.
KTMB said KTM Komuter services from Pulau Sebang to Batu Caves would terminate at Seremban station.
Passengers were encouraged to use alternative transport to continue their journeys.
"For passengers on Komuter train No. 2006 (Pulau Sebang-Batu Caves), the service will terminate at Labu station before returning to Seremban station.
"Passengers are encouraged to use alternative transport to continue their journeys.
"For passengers on trains No. 2012 and 2014, two Komuter train sets have been deployed to Kajang and Bangi stations to pick up passengers.
"They will then travel towards Batu Caves, stopping at the stations along the route," it said.
KTMB said passengers who chose not to continue their journey due to the disruption would be entitled to a full fare refund, subject to the applicable procedures.
Its technical teams were carrying out inspection and recovery work at the location to restore train services as soon as possible.
The repair work was estimated to take three hours.
Passengers were advised to plan their journeys and obtain the latest updates through KTMB's official channels, including its social media platforms and station staff.

619669093c028509: NAGOYA: Nagoya's mayor apologised to athletes on Wednesday for "inconveniences" at the Asian Games in the Japanese city following a string of complaints.
The continent's biggest sporting event has been dogged by problems including a shortage of beds and issues with transport.
There are over 17,000 athletes and officials, more than the Olympics, and countries have accused local organisers of mismanagement.
"We must offer our apologies to the athletes and others affected by these inconveniences," said Mayor Ichiro Hirosawa, who is also acting chairman of the local organising committee.
"We must sincerely reflect on the mishandling that occurred," he added.
"There were human errors and a lack of communication with the national teams.
"We are responding based on what has happened."
Unlike past Games, there is no athletes' village in a bid to save money, with participants instead sleeping in temporary wooden units, on a cruise ship and in hotels.
Some teams have complained about the temporary cabins, even saying the beds are too short.
Early in the Games local organisers apologised to South Korea after the North Korean national anthem was played by mistake.
There have been issues with buses for athletes not running when they should, not turning up at all or going to the wrong venues.
Some athletes were also stranded for hours at the airport when they landed in Nagoya for the start of the Games on September 19.
The Games, which are taking place in Nagoya and Aichi prefecture, end on Sunday.AFP
b510ac3b6190e9cf: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian household financial asset growth slowed to 6.2 per cent in 2025 from 8.7 per cent a year earlier, trailing both regional and global growth, according to Allianz Research.

Gross financial assets reached €769 billion (RM3.56 trillion), but grew at a slower pace than the 9.8 per cent average among surveyed Asian countries excluding Japan and China, and the global average of 8.6 per cent.
Insurance and pensions led the increase, rising 11.1 per cent, compared with 2.8 per cent growth in securities and 2.3 per cent in deposits.
Despite the stronger growth in insurance and pensions, Malaysian household wealth remained heavily concentrated in deposits and retirement savings.

Deposits and savings held in the Employees Provident Fund together accounted for 68 per cent of total financial assets, Allianz Research said in its Global Wealth Report 2026, which examines household assets and debt across almost 60 countries.
After adjusting for inflation, Malaysian financial assets grew 4.7 per cent in real terms in 2025, slowing from 6.7 per cent in 2024.
Since 2019, they have risen a cumulative 21.9 per cent in real terms, below the regional average of 39.6 per cent and the global average of 22.9 per cent.
Meanwhile, household liabilities increased 5.6 per cent to €360 billion (RM1.67 trillion), slower than the growth in assets.
This lifted net financial assets by 6.7 per cent to €409 billion (RM1.89 trillion).
Malaysia had net financial assets of €11,370 (RM52,643.10) per capita in 2025, ranking 39th among the world's richest countries covered by the report.
Globally, household financial assets rose 8.6 per cent to a record €268.4 trillion in 2025, with rising asset prices accounting for about four out of every five euros of new wealth.
"Global wealth set another record in 2025, but that only tells half of the story," Allianz Research chief economist and chief investment officer Ludovic Subran said.
"Since 2019, nominal financial assets are up 50 per cent, but in real terms, stripped of inflation, they only grew 23 per cent."
Securities were the fastest-growing asset class globally, rising 12.4 per cent, more than twice the growth in deposits at 5.7 per cent and insurance and pensions at five per cent.
Securities accounted for a record 46.9 per cent of global financial assets, reflecting the growing role of market investments in wealth creation.
8b1068556a2e39b8: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 30 — The government expects the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, Le Tour de Langkawi and Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon to proceed this weekend despite haze affecting several parts of the country, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.

eed5d37275d0416a: KUALA LUMPUR: Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd's share price fell over 14 per cent to RM3.70 by 3pm today, driven by heavy profit-taking following a fourfold gain in its stock price year-to-date.

01e78fe89c9ff7ec: NEW DELHI, Sept 30 — India’s capital goes to the dogs on Wednesday, as voters choose which of the city’s chubbiest canines deserves to be crowned its fattest.
The “Fat Dogs of Delhi” contest, in the style of Alaska’s annual Fat Bear Week, has turned Instagram into a virtual polling booth, attracting nearly 100,000 followers.
The competition, which began on September 24 with 64 dogs, culminates in a final round on Wednesday — complete with rival campaigns, posters and accusations of paid publicity.
Organisers, on the @fatdogsofdelhi Instagram account, say voting will also take place in person on Wednesday.
“Delhi’s heavyweight election gets ruff”, the Hindustan Times reported. “Serious Pawlitics”, The Print added.
The competition was thrown into disarray when frontrunner Gola — meaning “round”, a tubby brown hound — was reported to have died.
Voting is now down to its final round, pitting the late Gola, also known as “Kebab”, against Googoo, a hulking brown-and-white dog.
Organisers, who have stayed anonymous, said they were taken aback by the “dramatic spike in our social media followers” since its launch.
The site, which posted videos of the rotund hounds getting belly rubs, has posted details of animal charities “working to ensure that our furry little friends get a dignified life.”
There are tens of thousands of stray dogs in the capital.
In middle-class neighbourhoods, many of Delhi’s strays are beloved by residents, with some dogs even dressed in jackets during winter.
But the city’s media also regularly report on attacks by stray dogs, a crisis compounded by inadequate sterilisation programmes and legal restrictions on culling.
The Supreme Court last year ordered a mass roundup of dogs, before scaling back the operation after questions were raised over the feasibility of such a large-scale exercise.
The canine contest comes against the backdrop of more serious electoral politics.

The Election Commission of India, long regarded as the guardian of the world’s largest democracy, is facing scrutiny after a newspaper investigation alleged impropriety during a large-scale voter-roll revision.
The ECI, a constitutional body, has rejected the allegations, saying its decisions were unanimous and legally valid. — AFP
781008ff501c5bd6: BEIJING: Nearly two decades after stepping away from showbiz at the peak of her career, Taiwanese actress Joey Wong has finally shared why she chose to leave the scene in 2005.
The 59-year-old former star, who made her acting debut back in 1983, opened up during an episode of the Chinese talk show Follow Each Other, broadcast on Sept 23.
Speaking to host Li Dan, she admitted that fame never truly suited her.
"I was never really comfortable in the spotlight," she reflected. "I never quite understood what it meant to be an actress."
Wong explained that it was actually her mother who pushed her to join show business and make a name for herself.
But after several years in the industry, exhaustion set in. Questioning if there was more to life, she began turning down work.
"Everyone wants different things out of life," she said. "I felt I had done my bit by fulfilling my mother's wishes, and I knew she wouldn't expect anything more from me."
When asked if she ever missed acting, Wong laughed, saying the industry now felt completely foreign.
"I take things as they come. When good things arrive, I cherish them, and when they leave, I don't try to hold on. I know I was happy back then."
She also revealed that she hadn't consulted her close mentors—director Tsui Hark and the late producer Shi Nansheng—before walking away.
"My mind was made up. If I had discussed it with them, it would have turned into a long debate, and I was set on leaving."
Addressing long-standing rumours, Wong dismissed claims that heartbreaks drove her away from acting, and keeps details about past relationships private.
"People will make up stories whether I explain myself or not, so I prefer to stay quiet," she remarked. "I've made peace with how things turned out. I feel I've settled all my emotional debts."

After retiring, Wong moved to Canada to lead a quieter life. She later ventured into alternative health, opening a moxibustion centre in Vancouver in 2024, followed by a second branch in Silicon Valley in 2026.
Looking back on her filming days, Wong fondly remembered working alongside Hong Kong icons Leslie Cheung and Chow Yun Fat.
She recalled how Cheung, her co-star in A Chinese Ghost Story, helped ease her anxiety when she struggled with Cantonese on set.
Of Chow, her co-star in God of Gamblers, she admired his modesty.

"He would carry equipment for the crew and treat everyone with genuine kindness," she shared. "He showed me what a true star should be like, and I wanted to follow his example. He taught me a great deal."
fd1e0d3dbc7f477b: AICHI: Malaysia's Identity V squad will use their bronze medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games as motivation to chase gold when the country hosts the 2027 SEA Games.

Team captain Gan Hoon Ming admitted disappointment after their hopes of reaching the final were dashed, but said the experience of competing at the Asian Games gave the team added motivation to return stronger.
Malaysia had to settle for bronze after losing 2-0 to Japan in the semi-finals at the Aichi Sky Expo on Wednesday.
In the best-of-three format, the national squad went down 5-3 in the opening round before fighting back to hold Japan to a 4-4 draw in the second.
Japan then dominated the deciding round with an aggressive display to win 8-1 and book their place in the final.

Hoon Ming, who led a Malaysian line-up comprising Yiau Wen Feng, Vincent Yii, Nicky Ho, Ng Wei Hao, George Chin and Cheah Euggee, said facing Japan provided valuable experience against one of Asia's strongest teams.
"We actually had a chance to beat them, but we did not play well enough. Japan are a very strong team because they fielded their best players," said Hoon Ming.
"I am very honoured to have competed against them. It was a very close match because both teams were at a similar level."
Hoon Ming said Malaysia have now faced Japan three times, recording one win and two defeats, including Wedesday's semi-final.
He said playing against Japan's highly skilled players had helped the national squad identify areas that needed improvement.
"We will take this experience and use it to improve our game. We will try to do better after this," he said.
On winning bronze, Hoon Ming said the team were proud to deliver a medal for Malaysia, although they still believed they were capable of achieving more.
"We are very happy to have won a medal for Malaysia, but at the same time we are disappointed because we believe we could have done better," he said.
"Maybe we could have won gold or silver, but this is not the end. We will keep working to become better."
Hoon Ming said the team's main target now is to prepare for the 2027 SEA Games, where they will aim to win gold on home soil.

8a4afef579cbbf8a: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has allowed Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's bid to have five preliminary issues decided before a sexual assault civil suit filed by his former research aide, Muhammed Yusoff Rawther, proceeds to full trial.
Judge Datuk Raja Ahmad Mohzanuddin Shah Raja Mohzan ruled that the issues raised by Anwar were suitable to be determined first under Order 33 Rule 2 of the Rules of Court.

He said the events pleaded by Yusoff were sequential, as he must first establish that he was at Anwar's Segambut residence on Oct 2, 2018, before the alleged sexual assault or trespass to the person could have taken place in the study.
"If the preliminary issues are answered in the defendant's favour, the plaintiff's claim will come to an end.

"If they are answered in the plaintiff's favour, the findings will be final and binding, and the continuing trial will be confined to the alleged sexual assault and/or trespass to the person," he said today.
Raja Mohzanuddin said either outcome would result in substantial savings in time and costs.
The five preliminary issues include whether Anwar's then private secretary, Shukri Saad, instructed Yusoff to personally deliver a speech to Anwar's Segambut residence.
They also concern whether Yusoff travelled there with Anwar's security personnel, Norafee Ahmad, and whether he met Anwar at the residence that day.
The remaining issues concern whether the alleged sexual assault or trespass to the person could have occurred if Yusoff did not meet Anwar.
They also include whether Yusoff's writ and statement of claim would remain sustainable in law and fact.
The judge also held that Order 33 Rule 2 could apply to questions of fact, even where those facts were disputed.
He said Yusoff was not entitled to insist that every issue be determined only at a full trial.
However, Raja Mohzanuddin ruled that the preliminary issues could not be decided through affidavits alone.
He ordered a trial on the preliminary issues, with witnesses to give oral evidence and be subjected to cross-examination.
The judge also said Yusoff would be allowed to give evidence on the facts and particulars in the relevant parts of his statement of claim before the court turns to the preliminary questions.
The preliminary trial will be conducted via Zoom and remain open to the public.
Raja Mohzanuddin said the hearing would not be held in camera, adding that the principle of open justice could still be preserved through remote proceedings.
He also ordered all further proceedings in the suit to be stayed pending the determination of the preliminary issues.
The further conduct of the suit will depend on the outcome of those issues.
The judge set Nov 5 for case management before a new judge who will hear the preliminary trial, including directions on access to the Zoom hearing and the fixing of trial dates.
Yusoff filed the suit in 2021, alleging sexual assault and claiming the incident affected his mental health.
Anwar has denied the allegations and filed a counterclaim.
In his statement of defence filed on Sept 28, 2021, Anwar alleged that Yusoff had lied under oath to the authorities regarding his allegations.
Anwar, who filed his counterclaim on the same date, also alleged that Yusoff had fabricated the story to tarnish his political career and prevent him from becoming prime minister.
On Sept 9, 2022, the High Court here dismissed Yusoff's application to strike out several paragraphs in Anwar's statement of defence and counterclaim.

afaac6d707c07691: PETALING JAYA: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd’s (KTMB) Electric Train Service (ETS) and KTM Komuter passenger train services on the Batu Caves-Pulau Sebang route have been disrupted since 6.24am today after a 25 kV overhead line (OHL) was severed at Km 434.423 between the Batang Benar and Labu stations.

KTMB said preliminary checks indicated the incident was likely caused by “animal bridging”, where an animal comes into contact with both a live wire and an earth wire, creating an unintended electrical path that disrupts the OHL protection system and power supply.

“The incident disrupted the power supply along the route, causing delays to several services, while some services were terminated early to allow safe inspection and restoration work,” KTMB was quoted as saying by Bernama today.

KTMB has implemented several operational adjustments, including for ETS train EP9532 from JB Sentral to KL Sentral. The train will terminate at the Seremban station, and passengers will take buses to KL Sentral and intermediate stations.
For ETS train EP9523 from KL Sentral to JB Sentral, passengers will take a bus to the Seremban station before continuing their journey to their respective destinations.
“ETS passengers will take the shuttle buses provided at KL Sentral, Bandar Tasik Selatan and Kajang to the Seremban station before continuing their journey by ETS,” it said.

For KTM Komuter services, train No 2008 from Pulau Sebang to Batu Caves will terminate at the Seremban station, while train No 2006 on the same route will terminate at Labu station before returning to Seremban.
Passengers are advised to use alternative transport modes to continue their journey.

For trains No 2012 and 2014 from Pulau Sebang to Batu Caves, two Komuter sets have been deployed to the Kajang and Bangi stations to transport passengers to the stations along the route up to Batu Caves.
Passengers who choose not to continue their journeys due to the disruption will receive full fare refunds, subject to applicable procedures.
KTMB said its technical teams were inspecting and restoring the affected infrastructure, with services expected to resume as soon as possible.
“KTMB apologises for the inconvenience caused and thanks passengers for their patience and cooperation throughout the disruption,” it said.

529d808c5b5b023b: SEOUL, Sept 30 — A wayward shark has become an unlikely celebrity in South Korea, drawing massive crowds, earning plaudits from the local mayor and even moving the stock market.
The predator — believed to be a bull shark — popped up in an artificial waterway in the port city of Busan on South Korea’s southeast coast this month.
Coast guard boats tried to guide the animal back to the sea by spraying water on it, but the shark — affectionately nicknamed ‘Bukhangi’ by fans after the port — did not budge.
And while authorities wonder what to do next, the 3.5-metre (11.5-foot) visitor and the crowds it has drawn have provided an unexpected boon to the local economy.
Sales of shark-shaped ice cream bars jumped nearly 30 per cent at nearby convenience stores.
Busan Mayor Chun Jae-soo has thanked the shark for publicity that would otherwise have cost “trillions”.
In tribute to its contributions, Bukhangi was elected an honorary public relations ambassador for the city with a stonking 91 per cent of the vote.
Others are cashing in — shares in The Pinkfong Company, the studio behind the viral Baby Shark song, briefly surged more than seven per cent.
Bull sharks are usually found in subtropical and tropical waters.
Sharks venturing into South Korean waters is “not common at all”, said Kim Jin-koo, a professor of global fisheries at Pukyong National University.
“As water temperatures around South Korea have risen, it appears to have moved closer to the country’s coast,” Kim said.
The fish’s fame has also been accompanied by a flood of false rumours.

A few days after its appearance, authorities said that a second fish had been spotted in the area — prompting some social media users to suggest it was Bukhangi’s child and share AI-generated images purporting to show the pair.
An official at Busan’s park policy division told AFP that no additional sharks have been spotted since Bukhangi’s appearance.
They also said authorities would make another attempt at moving the shark on Friday.
The shark joins a list of unlikely animal celebrities in South Korea — most notably Neukgu, a young wolf that escaped from a zoo in April.
The lost pup spent nine days on the lam before being recaptured. — AFP
fe48ce1f57ff2bf0: SEREMBAN: A Form Two student who died after allegedly being bullied at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah on Friday was beaten with a rubber hose by two senior students before he was found unconscious.
According to Kosmo! Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the two Form Four students also repeatedly struck the soles of the victim's feet with the hose.
He said the incident occurred after Maghrib prayers when all students were supposed to attend a revision or 'prep' session at their respective hostels.
The victim, Muhammad Idlan Fareeq, 14, was believed to have been called by the two suspects after he was caught vaping, Alzafny said.
"The action by the two suspects is believed to have been a form of punishment imposed on the victim after he was caught vaping by a school warden on Sept 23," he said.
Alzafny said the suspects initially instructed the victim to get the rubber hose from the bathroom before taking him to a hostel room on the second floor.
He said the victim was believed to have been beaten first in the second suspect's room on the first floor before being taken to the main suspect's room on the second floor.
He said the victim was ordered to sit down before the soles of his feet were struck several times with the rubber hose.
"After that, the victim was asked to stand and remove his shirt before being hit with their hands on the front and back of his body until he fell," he said.
Alzafny said the injured victim was then laid on a bed, with one of the suspects attempting to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) after noticing that his condition was deteriorating.
He said the suspects then contacted a warden before Idlan was taken to Hospital Tuanku Ampuan Najihah (HTAN), Kuala Pilah where he was pronounced dead.
"However, we cannot determine whether the victim died at the hostel or on the way to the hospital," he said.
Alzafny said the two suspects were also the victim's classmates in archery.

It was reported that Idlan was rushed to HTAN before he was pronounced dead, with the case investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code which states that anyone found guilty of murder is subject to imprisonment of 30 to 40 years in prison.
The post-mortem has yet to determine the cause of death, with samples sent to the Chemistry department for analysis.
Police have so far recorded statements from 69 witnesses, comprising 53 students, four teachers, three wardens, six parents, two doctors and a boxing coach.
The first suspect was remanded for six days until tomorrow, while the second suspect was remanded from Sept 28 to Oct 3.
85a3ce19b26bb8d8: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Touch ‘n Go Sdn Bhd (Touch ‘n Go) is expanding its Enhanced Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) network with 10 additional lanes by the end of the year to support the country’s transition towards a Multi-Lane Fast Flow (MLFF) tolling ecosystem.

Its Chief Operations Officer Liza Woon Yin Yin said the expansion, announced in conjunction with Touch ‘n Go’s 30th anniversary, aligns with the company’s broader vision to support the government’s barrier-free tolling initiative by providing robust and proven technology.

“We are ready to support with the technology, and we’ll continuously improve. We have a total of 10 more new lanes by the end of the year to support and prove the technology that we have to ease up the whole toll mobility,” she told Bernama when met at the MyASEAN Roads & Traffic Tech Expo (MyARTTE) at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) here today.

The new lanes will be deployed across five highways, comprising two lanes each at the Putrajaya Toll Plaza on the Maju Expressway (MEX), Sungai Ramal Toll Plaza on the Kajang Dispersal Link Expressway (SILK), Bukit Raja Toll Plaza on the Grand Sepadu Highway, and Bukit Jelutong Toll Plaza on the Guthrie Corridor Expressway (GCE).
Another two lanes, one each, will be installed at the Sungai Long and Ampang Toll Plazas on the East Klang Valley Expressway (EKVE).
Currently, two Enhanced RFID lanes are already operational, located at the Ampang-bound Dato Keramat toll plaza on AKLEH, and the Putrajaya-bound Putrajaya toll plaza on the MEX Highway.
Woon said the RFID lanes feature an enhanced technology that utilises two RFID antennas paired with an Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) camera.

“It’s an enhanced technology with two RFID antennas, and together with the ANPR camera in the middle to support the front and also the back as a secondary RFID to strengthen the security and also the accuracy,” she said.
Woon also assured motorists of a much smoother drive-through experience, noting that the upgraded lanes will offer an experience similar to the targeted MLFF system.
Earlier, she took the media on a guided tour of Touch ‘n Go’s Connected Mobility pavilion, themed “Future of Malaysia’s Mobility, Built on 30 Years of Trust”.

Woon shared insights into the company’s 30-year milestone and technological advancements, while briefing the media on the Single Lane Fast Flow (SLFF) e-RFID, MLFF Titan Flow technology and Gold Star virtual reality (VR) experience.
Meanwhile, Touch ‘n Go, in a statement, said the 10 new Enhanced RFID lanes will be clearly indicated by a gold star symbol on the lane signage to help motorists identify them easily.

Unlike conventional lanes, the Enhanced RFID lanes incorporate components of Touch ‘n Go’s homegrown Titan Flow technology stack, combining enhanced RFID capabilities with artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning technologies.
This multi-technology approach significantly improves vehicle detection and lane throughput, enabling highly reliable toll transactions even at higher vehicle speeds. — Bernama
d6e7f1e458110a26: BEIRUT: The Lebanese military said on Wednesday that an Israeli strike on southern Lebanon wounded a soldier and three civilians, as the implementation of a deal between the two countries has stalled.
"A soldier was seriously wounded as the result of an Israeli targeting of an army vehicle," Nabatieh al-Fawqa, Lebanon's army, said in a statement, adding that three civilians were also injured.

Lebanon's state-run National News Agency reported that "an enemy drone attacked Nabatieh al-Fawqa", a town that has been under repeated Israeli strikes in recent weeks despite a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah.
The Israeli military did not immediately comment on the incident.

Iran-backed Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the broader Middle East war in March by attacking Israel, which responded with massive airstrikes and a ground invasion that Lebanon says has killed more than 4,300 people.

Lebanon and Israel concluded a framework agreement in June under US auspices, which involves the disarmament of Hezbollah, a gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanon's south and the deployment of the Lebanese army to the region, starting in test areas known as "pilot zones".
Violence has decreased since the signing of the agreement and of a US-Iran memorandum of understanding earlier that month.
Lebanon's military deployed in two of the "pilot zones" in July, but the implementation of the agreement has been stalled since then.
In his meeting with US secretary of state Marco Rubio in Washington on Wednesday, Lebanese prime minister Nawaf Salam pushed for the agreement to be further implemented.
Hezbollah, meanwhile, refuses to lay down its weapons, and Israel still carries out strikes on Lebanon and occupies land in its south despite the agreement.

bfb68b87c5928bee: PARIS: Climate change is increasingly reshaping the polar oceans, with Arctic waters warming rapidly, sea ice shrinking and wildlife losing habitat at both ends of the planet, an annual report said Wednesday.

The Copernicus Ocean State Report depicts profound changes across the world's seas, from record-breaking heatwaves in the Mediterranean and Black seas to shifts in marine ecosystems and increasingly acidic waters.
"The message is very clear. The ocean is changing rapidly," said Pierre Bahurel, director general of Mercator Ocean International, which runs the EU's Copernicus Marine Service.
Some of the more dramatic effects from global warming are taking place in the poles, which occupy around 20% of the global ocean surface.
The Arctic's combined sea surface and sea-ice surface temperature rose 4.2°C between 1982 and 2024, or around 1°C per decade, according to the 10th annual oceans report.
By comparison, global sea surface temperatures have been increasing by 0.12°C per decade.
In the Kara Sea north of Siberia, temperatures have climbed by 6.7°C since 1982, or 1.68°C per decade.
As temperatures rise, Arctic sea ice has shrunk by nearly half a million square kilometres per decade since 1979, equivalent to losing an area the size of Spain every 10 years.
The retreating ice exposes Arctic coastlines to waves, worsening coastal erosion and raising risks for coastal communities and infrastructure, the report warned.

"The Arctic sea ice has been declining since the early 80s, leaving around 60% of coastal infrastructure vulnerable to erosion and sea level rise," Karina von Schuckmann, director of the oceans report, said in a media briefing.
Ice loss in Antarctica, meanwhile, is threatening penguin populations on the frozen continent.
Record-low Antarctic sea ice in 2022 coincided with the first-ever recorded large-scale breeding failure of emperor penguins, the report said.
Emperor penguins rely on stable sea ice to live, hunt and breed, and their chicks can perish if they fall in freezing water before developing waterproof feathers.
In April, emperor penguins were upgraded from "near threatened" to "endangered" by the IUCN, the global authority on threatened wildlife.
More than 90% of emperor penguin colonies could be near-extinct by 2100 if sea ice loss persists at its current rate.

95505e538953bfba: PARIS, Sept 30 — Heatwaves and wildfires combined with human-caused emissions this year combined to expose one third of the world’s population to extremely high levels of ozone pollution, a European Union report said on Wednesday.

In a new analysis covering the first eight months of 2026, the European Union’s Copernicus Climate Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) highlighted the close relationship between climate change and air pollution.

When heat and sunlight react with airborne emissions from wildfires, vehicles and industry, they create ground-level ozone pollution, which can damage lung tissue, cause breathing problems, trigger asthma attacks and lead to other health issues.
Despite progress in cutting the most harmful air pollutants in recent decades, ozone has proved more difficult to tackle as climate change fuels the conditions that favour its formation.
This year’s ozone pollution was driven in part by record-breaking heatwaves and wildfires that seared Europe and North America and sent smoke well beyond their borders.

Indonesia has experienced major wildfires, while the warming El Nino weather pattern, which started in June and is due to peak later this year, could drive more fires in southeast Asia, according to the analysis.

“Air pollution does not stop at borders. It can travel thousands of kilometres, crossing continents and oceans and affecting air quality far from its source,” CAMS director Laurence Rouil said in the Atmosphere Watch report.
‘Extremely poor’ air
CAMS uses satellite data and computer models to track air pollution and wildfires.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The report found that 34 per cent of the global population was exposed to ‘extremely poor’ air quality between January 1 and September 15. — AFP pic

The report found that 34 per cent of the global population was exposed to “extremely poor” air quality between January 1 and September 15, meaning concentrations of ozone were well above the World Health Organization’s exposure guidance.
The WHO’s guideline sets 100 micrograms of ozone per cubic metre as the maximum recommended level of exposure, averaged over eight hours.
Another 17 per cent of the world breathed “very poor” air, while five per cent was exposed to “good” levels of ozone.
Asia has the highest rate of exposure to ozone pollution, with 53 per cent of its population breathing “extremely poor” air. Another 22 per cent was exposed to “very poor” ozone.
The continent’s widespread emissions are driven by industrialisation, economic development and transport, as well as wildfires and the burning of agricultural residue.
New Delhi, Dhaka, Chinese megalopolis Chongqing and Pakistan’s Lahore were among cities whose ozone levels were “extremely poor”.
Two thirds of the population in North America and 45 percent in Europe were exposed to “poor” or “very poor” air quality.
EU regulation has been effective in reducing emissions from air pollutants, except for ozone, the report said.
Ozone pollution is linked to 60,000 premature deaths per year in Europe, Ian Marnane, an official at the European Environment Agency, told a media briefing.
Ozone levels in North America also remained “relatively unchanged” despite ambitious emissions reduction policies, the report said.
Smoke from forest fires, crop burning and cooking are significant contributors to Africa’s air pollution while Saharan dust travels as far as Europe.
Eight per cent of Africa’s population endured “extremely poor” air quality this year. It was “very poor” or “poor” for 19 per cent of the continent.
Ozone levels were very high in the Brazilian city of Sao Paulo and extremely elevated in Rio de Janeiro but the air quality was “good” or “fair” for 81 per cent of South America’s population.
One bright spot was Oceania, including Australia and New Zealand, where 66 per cent of the population enjoyed “good” ozone levels and 34 per cent lived under “fair” conditions. — AFP

14fe4454c086a419: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has urged the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to initiate an investigation into Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi over an alleged RM2.1 billion budget overrun at the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW).

In a statement today, Lim said the anti-graft agency should apply the same rigorous enforcement standards to KKDW as it did in its recent probe into Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), where management was found to have channelled nearly RM260 million into its investment arm, UiTM Holdings, without the required approval from the Ministry of Finance.

Citing official Finance Ministry figures, Lim noted that KKDW spent RM1.8 billion in 2023 against an approved budget of RM1.1 billion. In 2024, the ministry expended RM2 billion against a RM1.3 billion allocation, followed by RM2.3 billion spent against an approved RM1.6 billion in 2025.

Lim said that the cumulative overspending totalled RM2.1 billion across the three-year period, all during Ahmad Zahid’s tenure as rural and regional development minister, stressing that unapproved overspending had not occurred prior to 2023.

“Such conduct by Ahmad Zahid Hamidi is irresponsible as it violates existing financial procedures and regulations, which could warrant enforcement under the relevant laws,” he said, adding that decisive action is essential to deter other federal ministries from committing similar fiscal breaches.

Lim warned that the MACC risks facing public accusations of selective prosecution and double standards if it hesitates to act against Ahmad Zahid and KKDW “because of his high position”, calling such inaction fundamentally unfair to the management of UiTM.

Lim pointed to findings by Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee (PAC), which discovered that UiTM management injected approximately RM260 million into UiTM Holdings in stages between 2007 and 2018 without Treasury clearance, resulting in accumulated losses of RM157.04 million across financial years 2017, 2018, 2019, and 2021.

According to the PAC, RM42 million designated for a 50-megawatt solar development in Gambang, Pahang, was diverted for unrelated operational expenses without the authorisation of the company’s board of directors.
Lim added that strict governance is needed to safeguard UiTM’s increased RM3.08 billion budget allocation for 2026.

7883b9b2ec0462f5: The Spectre microarchitecture vulnerability has returned yet again, this time to vex just-in-time (JIT) engines that generate machine code for browsers, runtimes, and kernels. The vulnerability is found in many CPUs that use speculative execution, the process of executing code before it is called to boost performance. Researchers found speculative execution opens the door to side channel attacks through which secrets can be exposed or inferred. When news of that risk became known, chipmakers and OS developers scrambled to fix these vulnerabilities, which were referred to as Spectre and Meltdown. And since then, researchers have found two or three dozen variations, such as 2025's VMScape, one of several so-called "Spectre v2" attacks that attempt to exploit indirect branch prediction, where program control is passed indirectly by pointing to an address where the next instruction can be found rather than specifying the instruction itself. The attacker trains the branch predictor to execute speculatively to a chosen address in order to leak data about the microarchitecture state. Researchers from Vrije Universiteit in the Netherlands and Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna in Italy have revived Spectre in a form called Branch Target Reuse (BTR), which they describe as the first practical in-place Spectre v2 attack that attacks just-in-time (JIT) compilers. An in-place attack is confined to the victim's branch while an out-of-place attack relies on speculation directed toward a target on a different branch. The researchers – Sander Wiebing, Yuhui Zhu, Alessandro Biondi, and Cristiano Giuffrida – found that this novel Spectre form can be conjured from code left in JIT engines including Linux cBPF, Oracle GraalVM, and Mozilla SpiderMonkey. "The key insight behind the attack is that, while modern CPUs restore architectural code coherence after self-modification, they do not necessarily invalidate stale indirect branch prediction entries (i.e., branch targets)," the authors explain. "In JIT engines, these stale targets can outlive the original code and later be reused when the code cache is repopulated, yielding a speculative execute-after-free primitive." The result is that an attacker can commandeer speculative control flow in a way that avoids some software defenses like FineIBT [PDF]. The authors showed they could exploit this flaw by designing two proof-of-concept exploits against an Intel-based Linux kernel that reveal the root password hash even with the constant binding defense provided by cBPF. The expected leakage rate is 5.7 KB/sec for Intel Raptor Cove chips and 5.4 KB/sec for Lion Cove. It's slow but enough for an unprivileged user to coax a sensitive password hash out of a vulnerable system. After the researchers disclosed their findings, Linux kernel developers and Oracle put mitigations in place. Two CVEs were assigned: CVE-2026-64507 and CVE-2026-64508. Mozilla, the researchers said, has opted to prioritize work on site isolation instead of addressing the issue directly. Strong mitigations like IBPB are said to be effective but add complexity and hinder performance. The Branch Target Reuse paper has been accepted for publication at the ACM Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS) 2026, which will be held November 15 through 19 in The Hague, Netherlands. ®

11c2cf8ead728b53: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 30 — The Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia (ACCCIM) has proposed RM1,900 a month as an “appropriate” minimum wage, warning that a substantially larger increase could put pressure on smaller businesses and drive up consumer prices.
In a statement today, ACCCIM president Datuk Ng Yih Pyng said the proposed RM1,900 rate would represent an 11.8 per cent increase from the current minimum wage of RM1,700.
He said any adjustment should balance higher incomes for workers against the ability of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to absorb rising labour costs.

“An appropriate level of minimum wage is RM1,900 per month, an increase of 11.8 per cent from the current RM1,700,” Ng said, adding that minimum wage increases must balance improvements in workers’ incomes against “the operational survival of MSMEs”.
ACCCIM said it was not opposed to raising the minimum wage, but cautioned that an excessively large increase could deliver a cost shock to businesses already operating on thin margins.

It said some businesses could pass the additional costs on to consumers through higher prices, while labour-intensive sectors such as retail, restaurants, food services, agriculture and small- and medium-sized manufacturing would be particularly exposed.

The chamber also argued that an increase in the wage floor could have a “ripple effect” on workers earning slightly above the minimum wage, while raising employers’ statutory contributions to the Employees Provident Fund (EPF), Social Security Organisation (Socso) and Employment Insurance System (EIS).

It warned that a one-size-fits-all approach could force some smaller businesses to reduce their workforce or shut down, and called for future increases to take into account productivity and performance, the financial capacity of individual sectors and wider economic and business conditions.

ACCCIM also urged the government to consider a tiered regional minimum wage system, arguing that differences in living costs, labour-market conditions and economic development meant a single nationwide rate might not suit every state.

“A uniform national minimum wage cannot be one-size-fits-all,” the chamber said, adding that wage levels should take into account regional differences in the cost of living, socioeconomic factors and business development.

It said a regional system could allow higher wages in more expensive urban centres while protecting low-margin businesses in economically weaker areas from unsustainable labour-cost increases and potential job losses.

Malaysia’s RM1,700 monthly minimum wage took effect on February 1, 2025 for employers with five or more workers and employers carrying out professional activities, regardless of workforce size. It was extended to all employers from August 1, 2025.
f29208c33672140c: PETALING JAYA: The Cabinet has agreed to exempt micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) from further increases in minimum wage for the time being, says entrepreneur development and cooperatives minister Steven Sim.
Sim said while the Cabinet agreed in a meeting today that wages needed to be increased, the government had to protect MSMEs, which are facing operating cost pressures and economic challenges.

"The government will take other approaches to increase the wages of workers in the MSME sector, including wage subsidies under the Progressive Wage Policy, so that wage increases come in tandem with productivity increases.
"Our goal is clear: worker welfare must be protected with more reasonable wages, while MSMEs remain competitive to continue expanding and generating employment opportunities," he said.

In August, human resources minister R Ramanan said the government was reviewing the RM1,700 minimum wage, with a final decision on maintaining or raising the amount to be made by the National Wages Consultative Council.
He said the review would consider basic economic indicators such as the poverty line and median wage, as well as inflation, labour productivity and the unemployment rate.
The RM1,700 minimum wage has been in force since August 2025 and applies to all workers in Malaysia except domestic workers.

cca47414faf3f2dd: PETALING JAYA: Umno mempersoalkan kritikan PKR Negeri Sembilan berhubung kemelut institusi dan pentadbiran negeri, yang menurutnya dibuat tanpa melihat rentetan peristiwa membawa kepada keadaan sekarang.

Sufian berkata, kerajaan negeri ketika ini perlu diberikan ruang untuk menyelesaikan kemelut berkenaan secara tertib, berperlembagaan dan menghormati proses yang sedang berjalan.
Menurutnya, perkara membabitkan institusi diraja, adat dan struktur pemerintahan Negeri Sembilan tidak seharusnya dijadikan medan untuk mencetuskan tekanan politik.
